title: Serum-marker model mSTOP flags NSCLC non-responders to checkpoint inhibitors
summary: The longitudinal machine learning model mSTOP, based on serum CEA and Cyfra 21-1, identified 35.1% of non-responding patients with a positive predictive value of 84.8% in a dual-center validation cohort of 242 metastatic NSCLC patients, comparable to CT imaging. Combined with CT, PPV rose to 95.7% and 19.8% of non-responders were identified. Clinical and financial impact come from a discrete event simulation, not from observed outcomes.
ai_technology: Longitudinal machine learning model (mSTOP) on serial CEA and Cyfra 21-1 serum tumor markers

evidence.tested: Dual-center retrospective validation cohort (n=242) and a simulation of clinical and financial impact.
evidence.unknown: Observed effects on treatment decisions and costs, and performance in routine laboratory operation; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Flags early non-response to immune checkpoint treatment from marker trajectories.
